review.notes: Triage review of all 60 physical pages (printed numbering is offset: physical p.5 = printed 45). Full structural scan: all 10 code fences (5 pairs, appendix RBRM python/go listings) are balanced; the 13 image embeds carry the dialog figures (Figures 1-6, 9-10), so their internal prompt/completion text ('Full completion in Appendix...', the anthrax-toxin example, the AZD0530 tool trace) is figure-internal and present as images. Automated normalized 4-gram containment of every PDF page's text layer against the OCR markdown (word-level long-run analysis); low-containment pages resolve to either figure-internal text or the dropped footnote bodies listed under unresolved. Rendered and visually inspected physical p.5 (printed 45, footnote 7/8 region, 300 dpi crop), p.25 (printed 65, Figure 8) and p.26 (printed 66, footnotes 31/32): the PDF text layer is reliable for this card (no hidden-character issues), so the missing footnote bodies can be transcribed mechanically from the text layer and spot-verified at 300 dpi. Line-by-line review was done only on the diff contexts of flagged pages; tables (e.g. p.6/p.7 race/sexuality tables), the RBRM appendix listings and most chart pages were machine-scanned only. The odd caption tail 'fixes to plot legend and title' on Figure 8 is printed in the PDF itself (visually verified on rendered physical p.25) and was correctly kept by the OCR. No patches were feasible within this review's budget: footnote restoration is a dedicated wave (see unresolved). Reviewer rendered p.5/25/26 to confirm footnote presence in print and text-layer fidelity; fn 2,3,4,8,10,11,13,16,17,20,24-26,28 survived in the OCR, the rest were dropped.

unresolved.evidence: OCR kept some page-bottom footnote bodies but dropped 15 of them wholesale (markers survive inline in the body text): fn1 p2 ('This document takes inspiration from the concepts of model cards and system cards...'), fn5 p3 ('Autonomously replicate is a reference to self-replication...'), fn6 p4 ('This categorization is not intended to represent an optimal, hierarchical taxonomy...'), fn7 p5 ('Note that, in addition to red teaming focused...'), fn9 p6 ('We use the term hallucinations...'), fn12 p7 ('Terms like harmful or toxic...'), fn14 p10 ('We focus here on disinformation...'), fn15 p12 ('We focus here on unconventional weapons...'), fn18 p13 ('For example, the model repeats many popular misconceptions about radioactivity.'), fn19 p15 ('Intuitively, systems that fail to preserve their own existence...'), fn21 p16 ('SMILES refers to Simplified Molecular Input Line Entry System') + fn22 p16 ('The red teamer attempted to purchase one of the proposed chemicals...'), fn23 p19 ('OpenAI's Charter states...'), fn27 p21 ('Mitigations and measurements were mostly designed, built, and tested primarily in English...'), fn29 p24 ('Real Toxicity Prompts is a dataset of 100k sentence snippets...'), fn31+fn32 p26 ('We will be sharing more about this work in a forthcoming publication.' / 'Content classifiers cannot fix all issues related with content harms...'). All bodies are cleanly recoverable from the PDF text layer (fidelity visually verified on rendered physical p.5, p.26 at 300 dpi); each needs a unique insertion anchor in the OCR markdown and a render check before becoming a patch. Word counts 10-270; several bodies run 100-270 words.

Chart-heavy pages (Figure 7 metrics, p.27 containment 0.05) and the p.6/p.7 discrimination tables were machine-scanned only; figure-internal axis text explains most low containment, but no table was verified cell-by-cell against a render.
